evidence.E1: The split is structural, not commentary: src/webhookd/app.py:379-421 ends the request at the commit and returns 202; src/webhookd/worker.py is a separate thread pool driven by `store.claim` (store.py:368-414) with leases, backoff and dead-lettering; the only coupling is the `on_accept=self.worker.notify` callback wired at app.py:535. `worker.enabled = false` plus a separate `webhookd worker` process is a supported deployment (src/webhookd/wsgi.py:9-16, README lines 314-328).

unanticipated_findings: CONFIRMED by execution: the same delivery can be handed to `handle()` by two worker threads *concurrently*, which directly contradicts the handler contract documented at src/webhookd/handlers.py:22-23 ("`handle` may be called concurrently from several worker threads. Never for the same event, but for different ones."). `Store.claim` (src/webhookd/store.py:386-387) re-claims rows where `status = 'processing' AND lease_expires_at <= ?`, so any handler that outlives `worker.lease_seconds` gets stolen while still running. Repro: create a Store, `record()` one delivery, run `Worker(store, SlowHandler, WorkerConfig(concurrency=2, lease_seconds=0.3, poll_interval=0.1, batch_size=1))` where SlowHandler sleeps 1.5s and records overlapping entries/exits. Output: `handle() invocations for the same delivery: 2` / `concurrent overlaps detected: [1]`. The README's at-least-once section (lines 221-231) covers sequential redelivery but not concurrent double-execution, and neither README nor the config example warns that `lease_seconds` (default 60) must exceed the slowest handler run — only a passing comment in config.example.toml line 39 ("must exceed your slowest handler run") hints at it. Consequence for a non-idempotent handler (e.g. the shipped `JsonlHandler`) is duplicated work — the exact thing the brief asks to prevent, just displaced from ingest to processing. No test in the suite covers lease expiry with a still-running handler.

Minor, reproducible: `webhookd sign <sender>` builds its example curl URL from `config.server.host`/`config.server.port` only (src/webhookd/cli.py:383), so it ignores a `--port` override passed to `webhookd serve`. Repro: `webhookd serve --config config.toml --port 8099` then `webhookd sign acme --body '{"order": 42}' --config config.toml` — the printed command targets `http://127.0.0.1:8080/hooks/acme` and fails against the running server. `--url` exists as a workaround but the README quick start (lines 30-45) pairs `serve` and `sign` without mentioning it.

Minor: `service.expose_stats` defaults to `true` with an empty `stats_token` (src/webhookd/config.py:123-124 and config.example.toml lines 19-20), so `GET /stats` publishes total/backlog/per-sender delivery counts to anyone who can reach the port. `webhookd check` warns (`warning:  /stats is exposed without a token; set service.stats_token if it is reachable`) but the service starts and serves it regardless — a secure-by-default choice would have been to require the token or default `expose_stats` to false.
